items.note: Association organized 1889 at Larrow Green; Gideon Vose first president to 1911; creamery built 1891 (story 1).
Article VII quoted verbatim, including 'the test of the station where he delivers shall govern' (story 1).
'Under payment by weight, nothing in the seven stories that follow would have cost any man a dollar.'
Loomis secretary 1901 and record's custodian (story 1); Teague bookkeeper 1905 (story 5); Sill buttermaker at Larrow Green (story 2).
'Selby Vose, manager, son of Gideon' (story 7); manager 1913 (story 5).
Station-gain line: 'The line runs annually from 1898', cream heavier than the books, ~5 1/4 per cent, carried to the general account (story 5).
Built winter 1895-96, seven miles up the valley, opened 4 May 1896 on glass borrowed from Larrow Green.
Weighing at intake, ten-day composite jar per patron, charge drawn to the mark, fat read in per cent off the rulings (story 3).
Ammon & Sons, Dairy Supply, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897.
Invoice reproduced in full: 6 doz. pipettes 17.6 c.c., 12 doz. bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
'a gap of 0.19 of a point, flat in July and February alike' (story 3); 'a standing gap of 0.19 in every month' (story 4).

LOST. Section A never states that a pipette cannot be checked without a burette, nor that none existed in the county. The full claim is made at F1 ('in the ordinary practice of the trade the pipette is the standard... caught only by a burette brought in from outside'), and the key forbids credit traveling from B-G into A. Story 8's '1921 the state began issuing graduated burettes' is the program, not the claim.
Born 1861, tester 1896-1924, twenty-nine seasons, dismissed 30 April 1925, died 1934.
Five-column book (date, patron, pounds, test, fat), one hand for 29 seasons, errors struck through and initialed, never written over.
Summary leaf quoted: 1896 3.80; 1897 part year; 1898 3.61 and within three hundredths ever since. Both figures present.
Broke 8 May 1911, borrowed measure to 10 July, 3.80 through the interval, fell the day the station's own measure returned, question mark set against it.
'Emmet Brant, the station's largest patron and Orra's brother'; brother-in-law estrangement after 1919 (story 7).
June 1919 circular over the manager's signature; the nine-sentence statement - tested as taught, cannot tell why, never took a pound of cream.
'died in 1934 with the imputation on him' (story 7). Book's later custody unbolded context.
Six farms on the wet meadow (story 4); Emmet Brant the largest patron (story 7).

LOST. Brant's weigh book appears in Section A only as a title in Ivy's list of five records. Its 1 January 1897 start and the two-scales-agree finding appear only at C2 ('by my own scale and theirs agreeing'), which cannot travel into A.

'From 1902 the men of the Hollow said out loud that their milk tested below... at Larrow Green.' The 0.17 (Hollow vs Green) and 0.19 (true shortfall) are explicitly kept apart at E Group 3, so the conflation gate holds.
Grigg committee, January-February-March 1908, wet-hay finding reported as the committee's finding and then defeated.
LOST. Brant's 1910 year (200,000 lb at a recorded 3.42) and the proportionality of the loss (4.56 short 0.24, 3.42 short 0.18) appear only at C1b/C2 and F1 - never inside Section A.
LOST. Section A never traces the weigh book to Roy Brant in 1929 or its loan to Ivy in 1958; the Hessel Bottom -> Roy -> Hazel chain appears only in Section E.
Cheese factory at Alder Corners, far side of Redlow Ridge, Vessey County, built by Jerome Cudd. Year does not gate; the asserted 1913 is charged as a corruption deduction instead.
'From 1915, four of the six Hessel Bottom men hauled to him in the summer flush... and went back down to their own station the rest of the year.'
Independence with all four elements: another county, his own bench, his own glass, and a book never compared with anybody's.
Sixteen seasons 1915-1930; 3.78-3.82 mean 3.80 against the same men's 3.61 at home; 'a difference of about 0.19'.
Same men's milk off the same wet ground in the flush kills the hay theory ('when the hay theory predicts none at all'); Rosalie's curd evidence and sixteen undocked summers kill watering.
'his daughter Rosalie'; 'figures copied out for Ivy Keddie in 1958'; her 1958 letter with the table of sixteen seasons.
'Merle Strawn, state dairy inspector on the Ordell circuit 1907-1936' - the 1907 pole taken, NT-23 avoided.
Lactometer for added water at every plant (story 8); 'tested for added water at that station on every visit and never found any' (story 7).
12 June 1923, pipettes run against the burette, 'Condemned the lot, the whole crate of them'.

LOST (closest call on the sheet). Story 8 gives 'He drew no inference at all about the twenty-six years behind it', but never states the bolded element - that he wrote no figure for the deficiency and made no report beyond the condemnation. The quoted entry happens to contain no figure; the sheet does not say so.
Ordered 28 June, entered by Ammon 2 July, new glass in use from July, 1924 'their book gives the year at 3.80' - r08's 3.90 avoided.
Crate up the ladder into the loft over the intake room; Strawn's notebooks 'at Farland since 1947'.
'In January 1925 the patrons petitioned.' Date carries the item.
Board under Frick; sat three times, 17 March at Ashlin and twice more in the station's own weigh room; reported 4 May 1925.
Water (Vose), theft by the tester (Teague), the hay read in from the 1908 report; 'None was proved.'

LOST. Section A gives 'four exhibits before the board and nothing else' but never names the four, and never names Strawn's 1923 notebook among them. The irony - Exhibit 4 held the answer and was read for its other lines - is made only at F1, which cannot travel into A.
Dismissed 30 April 1925, four days before the report, no finding then or ever; award 4 May, $3,800, without admission, charged to the station account.
'$3,800 awarded against a real loss of $19,000 - one fifth', charged to the station account (its own aspect under the A1.6/A7.6/A8.6 split).
Ivy Keddie, born 1931, Ansel's granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland; Professor Leland Vaught.
'the first person to bring five sets of records into one room' - test book, weigh book, Alder Corners figures, Strawn's notebooks, Association ledgers.
February 1958, climbed the loft ladder, nine pipettes unbroken - NT-16's eleven avoided.
9 March 1958, nine pipettes five runs each, mean 16.72 against 17.6, short 0.88, 'ninety-five hundredths of the mark'.
Bulletin quoted for 1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923 at one part in twenty; 3.61/3.80/0.19 and the 5 per cent error stated inside Section A (stories 2, 3, 6).

All four required elements inside Section A: 40,000,000 lb over the 25 full years 1898-1922; 76,000 lb; $19,000 at 25 cents; and the same 76,000 lb standing in the Association's ledgers as station gain (story 5 plus the Bulletin 471 quotation in story 8).
Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, clearing him; 35 years from condemnation, 33 from dismissal, 24 after his death.
Granddaughter.
Ansel -> Duncan -> Ivy, with Duncan's and Ivy's own statements, and Falke's printed retraction as the tie-breaker.
Second cousins, derived: Emmet and Orra siblings -> Roy and Duncan first cousins -> Hazel and Ivy their children.
'This cannot be determined from the sources, and it does not change the count' - correct abstention with the does-not-matter clause. Also declined again at E Group 4.
Gideon Vose, his father; nephew story named and rejected.
Gideon wrote Article VII, whose last clause made the station's own reading final; the accuser was enforcing his father's rule against a fault in the instrument that rule made decisive.

Scored as a correct abstention (borderline). The headline is 'No relationship... is established' - an epistemic frame, not a verdict on the world - and the close is 'Strictly, the sources cannot prove the absence of a remote connection'. Falls under 'leans one way while explicitly declining to decide'.

Two narrators assert cousinship from self-labelled valley talk and are shown to be one body of talk; Duncan denies it from inside the household; 'No genealogy, no record, no third party supports the claim.'
16.72 / 17.6 = 0.95; 95 per cent of true; short 0.88, one part in twenty.
3.61 / 0.95 = 3.80; shortfall 0.19; notes it is 5 per cent of 3.80, not a constant.
76,000 x $0.25 = $19,000; $3,800 paid; 3,800/19,000 = 0.20, 'exactly one fifth'. Both money and fraction.
360 x $0.24 = $86.40, with the 1910 price sourced to the Brant household and $90.00 flagged as the alternative.
76,000 = 5.00% of delivered and 5.26% of credited, denominators named explicitly and the specimen year worked; NT-20 identified as Teague's and Vaught's slip rather than adopted.
Lines summed to $77.93, and $77.39 broken by adding up Ammon's own reproduced invoice.
Six dozen = 72 pipettes, each short 0.88 c.c.; five dozen defeated by 72 x $0.35 = $25.20.

Both figures and the reason given: in use 1 May 1897 - 12 June 1923, money over the 25 full years 1898-1922, with the part-year explanation. The stated equivalent '26 years, 1 month and 12 days' is one day over the key's 26 y 1 m 11 d / 42 days, but the dates and the two-span distinction - the printed gate - are exact.
'The first season's intake: cannot be determined from the sources', with the accession note and both unsupported recollections. Correct abstention (A02).
The variable named: the measuring vessel, broken 8 May, borrowed until 10 July.
Constants listed well beyond three: patrons, herds, pasture, season, feed, acid, bottles, hand tester, scales, building, supervision, the man.
Rose to 3.80 on the first morning, held nine weeks, fell to 3.61 the day the station's measure returned. Nine weeks, NT-12 avoided.

Both halves: eliminates herds, ground, feed, season, weather and both honesty theories; and four stated limits, including that it does not say which glass was true, does not fix the magnitude across the period, and does not say why the glass was short.

Three reasons - ledger direction (Teague's own entry, Rundle's retraction), the 1911 interval (station book), the 1923-24 chronology (Strawn's field book and Keddie's book) - each attributed, across more than three narrators.
'Why these are independent' - three custodies, three record types, three kinds of argument; and 'Which survive without the 1958 measurement. All three.'

LOST (A09 asserted). Headline verdict: 'Once, obliquely, and never again', taking Teague's own 1916 account as settled. The key requires that whether the bookkeeper ever questioned the entries cannot be determined; the sheet never cites the clerk's opposing 'never asked anybody anything' or the absence of paper either way. -2 also applied.
'He certainly knew the tests ran low, and had known for years', with the 1926 address, the 1919 circular and the standing grievance.
Four of the five required observations: manager from 1913, signed the annual sheet carrying the line, wrote the 1919 circular, argued watering at the hearing (F1).

'What he understood by the station gain line cannot be determined', plus three of the five supporting observations - the two office men answering oppositely, neither documented, the signature proving presence not reading, and the 1926 address being after the fact.

Capped. Rows resolved with method: the 1924 average (3.80), six farms, Orra's 1866 by Duncan's own arithmetic, the crate in the loft, Ammon 'nothing before 1900', Nym's swapped keepers, the cheese factory's founding.

Capped. An eighteen-row table that names both carriers of each wrong value and the breaker - 16.27/16.72, five dozen, $77.39, eleven pipettes, 12 July, 1 May 1898, 44M, 3.16, six weeks, two tenths, 27 cents, $3,500, nephew, first cousin once removed, great-niece, niece, 67,000, $19,600.

A10 (the year Article VII was adopted) and A06 (whose measure was borrowed) both declared unsettleable with what is established. A04 (accident or substitution) is never declared unsettleable - Ammon's reground-mould account is attributed and D1 notes the works books burned, but no cannot-settle statement is made.

Group 2 identifies nine narrators refuting themselves on the page, including Vaught's cascade, Ammon's 1900 claim, Grigg's covering letter, Nym's catalogue, Duncan's 1868, Frick's 'every appliance', Strawn's twenty-eight books.
Composition 3+3+2+1 = 9, capped at 8.

Cause and size: the 1897 Ammon pipettes, 16.72 against 17.6, neck ruled for one charge, 95 per cent of the truth; 0.19 derived as 5 per cent of 3.80 and called a proportion; onset 1 May 1897 against the 1896 borrowed-glass 3.80, cessation 12 June 1923 and the 1924 3.80, with nothing on the farms changing at either end.
Watering named to Vose and Sill and defeated by the lactometer runs from 1907, Alder Corners, the cheesemaker's curd, the ledger direction and Vose's own chronology.

Theft named to Teague, Toland, Rundle and Oram's father and defeated by the cream arriving heavy in the accuser's own ledger, the 1911 interval, and the 1923-24 correction while Keddie was still at the bench.
Bog hay named to Grigg's 1908 committee and Kepp and defeated by Bulletin 214's five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer, the flat monthly shape, the three-month sample, and Alder Corners.

LOST (A07 asserted). The passage opens 'did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware? No.' - a headline verdict sentence with no declining qualifier. The key allows leaning negative on exactly this evidence only while explicitly declining to decide. -2 also applied.

LOST (A05 asserted). 'On the record, that he did not know', then 'My reading: he suspected the glass in 1911, correctly, could not prove it...' - the sheet picks the son's recollection over Frick's. Declining it in the Section E list does not save the item: the key scores A05 where the question is put. -2 also applied.
150 words by standard count (the standalone em dash excluded); at the cap. The sheet's own claim of 147 is low.

LOST. Only three of the nine record series are named: the by-law, the Association's ledgers, and the 1958 measurement. The test book, the invoice, Brant's weigh book, the Alder Corners book, Strawn's notebooks and the arbitration minutes are all absent; 'It took eight records' names none of them.

Scored as key item G1.3, no absorbed corruption (schema id retained). Watering, theft and the hay all appear as suspicion or blame, never as fact; every headline figure is right - 3.80, 17.6, 16.72, 3.61, 76,000, $19,000.

Four of six with both ends: 95 per cent of the truth (one part in twenty), May 1897, 76,000 lb / $19,000, and 1958. Missing: 1923 and the accident, and both Keddie names ('their tester', 'a granddaughter') - only four are required.

deductions.basis: 'Ansel Keddie went up in 1895 to get it ready' is asserted flatly. corruption-map X03/X64 plant exactly this sentence; the corrected value is 4 May 1896 and the station did not test before it opened. The sheet dates his testing correctly to 1896 but never flags the 1895/1896 near-tie pair anywhere.

deductions.item: F104/F049 - the station-gain line as Teague's own device from 1905
deductions.where: Section A story 5 ('Teague, on coming in in 1905, set the two against each other'; 'Teague's device from 1905') and D2 ('Teague invented the station-gain line himself in 1905')
deductions.basis: corruption-map X19; the line was carried from 1898 and he inherited it. The sheet prints both 1898 and 1905 without noticing r05's self-refutation, and never lists this among its self-refuting narrators.

'Jerome Cudd built a cheese factory at Alder Corners... in 1913' stated in the sheet's own voice. Key A5.1 is explicit that asserting 1913 as fact still takes the deduction though it no longer loses the item. Borderline: Section E later calls the 1913/1914 split 'not decisively settled' and distinguishes built from opened.

deductions.item: A09 - did the bookkeeper ever question the entries
deductions.basis: 'Once, obliquely, and never again.' - headline verdict in the sheet's own voice; no declining sentence anywhere.

deductions.item: A06 - whose measure was borrowed in 1911
deductions.where: Section A, story 6 ('borrowed, and brought up from Larrow Green with the cream wagon'; 'the borrowed measure came from Larrow Green')
deductions.basis: Flat assertion in Section A. Under the collision rule the E-c abstention still earns its point, but the -2 applies anywhere in the answers.

deductions.item: A07 - did the 1925 board examine the condemned glassware
deductions.basis: 'did the 1925 board ever examine the condemned glassware? No.' - verdict sentence with no declining qualifier.

deductions.item: A05 - what the tester himself believed
deductions.basis: 'On the record, that he did not know' and 'My reading: he suspected the glass in 1911, correctly' - the sheet resolves the two single-witness recollections in favour of the son. The Section E cross-reference does not decline it where the question is put.
